summary: A 1855 granite tower on a seabird island off Milbridge, Maine, at the foggiest station the Lighthouse Service measured; automated in 1972 and now in a wildlife refuge.

lens.where: moved to Rockland, Maine after 1972 automation (Shore Village Museum per the NRHP nomination; Maine Lighthouse Museum per LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: First tower, 25 ft per NRHP nomination; gone
109 ft per the NRHP nomination; 119 ft per LighthouseFriends and the USLHS archive

access.note: Island closed to the public April 1 to August 31 for seabird nesting; boat tours view it from the water; no public landing facilities described.

facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (island); U.S. Coast Guard maintains tower and aids

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination names Jeremiah Leighton from payroll ledgers; the USLHS archive and LighthouseFriends name Robert Upton (1817-1821), with Robert Leighton 1825-1832. Not resolved.
1817 is the first tower, 1855 the present one; the NRHP nomination also dates a rebuild of the first tower to 1823-1825.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the text: first keeper (Upton vs Jeremiah Leighton); first woman keeper claim (NRHP says paid; LighthouseFriends says denied); tower height (109 ft NRHP vs 119 ft); fog bell 1852 vs 1853; second dwelling 1875 vs 1876; steam to air whistle 1917 (LF) vs diaphragm horn 1938 (NRHP); lens museum name; flashing from 1855 (LF) vs 1857 (NRHP). LighthouseFriends dates the Valdare/Caldare schooner wreck to 1919; the 1929 Bulletin gives 4 August 1929 (volume year; keepers match the roster). Vessel names from Bulletin OCR (Northern Light, the 1928 sloop, the 1929 schooner) are garbled and uncertain, so the story gives only the first. The 1923 item is in the October 1, 1923 issue, 8 August 1923. The roster comes from the USLHS archive page; roster lines for USCG crew (1950s to 1972) are included as the archive prints them, not narrated. Newspapers (Chronicling America) held mostly notices to mariners; only the 1890 Ellsworth American item was used. Lighthouse Board volume labelled 1891 is ambiguous between fiscal years so was not used. The 1893 fog-test appendix is cited by scan page 722; printed page unconfirmed. Whether the Uptons were related is not stated. No photos verified. Current ownership of the tower (Coast Guard vs Fish and Wildlife) is stated differently by LighthouseFriends and the Friends of Maine Coastal Islands; visit status should be rechecked with the refuge. Fact-check 2026-10-27: 1893 fog-test passage is in the report volume labelled 1894 (scan p.722); the Petit Manan trial itself is dated November 1893. LF's 1919 date for the Caldare wreck is contradicted by the 1929 Bulletin and is now stated in the text.
